comparison: Subtract the conditional mean given the TRUE-support coordinates x_S* from y, and use the source model identity to obtain y-beta*^T*x. condExp with the sigma-algebra generated by x_S* supplies this residual under integrability and valid measurable-space hypotheses; its exceptional zero value is not a replacement for a missing conditional mean. The sample residual uses the true beta*, not an estimated candidate coefficient. Orthogonality to true-support coordinates follows only with the needed product integrability and conditional-expectation pull-out property; no independence or zero correlation with the remaining coordinates is asserted.
gap: Conditional expectation and subtraction express the true residual, retaining the true-support conditioning and required moment hypotheses.
searches: Inspect condExp/comap and the conditional-expectation pull-out theorem against the source true residual
The construction gives a conditional-mean residual, while covariance orthogonality needs product integrability and does not extend to covariates outside the conditioning support.

comparison: Form the coordinate subset of [p] where the SUM over environments of E[x_j^(e)*epsilon^(e)] is nonzero. A nonzero common uniform-weight factor would not change this set when the environment set is nonempty, but cancellation among signed environment moments does matter. G is therefore not the union of coordinates with a nonzero moment in at least one environment. Use integrable residual-covariate products to interpret the real expectations, retain complement relative to [p], and keep the later nonempty-G scope separate rather than building it into the definition.
gap: Real integrals, finite sums and a nonzero predicate express pooled spuriousness without replacing it by environmentwise spuriousness.
searches: Inspect the real integral and compare the defining nonzero sum with the saved pooled-cancellation qualification
The source takes signed moments before testing the pooled sum; generic integration neither prevents cancellation nor guarantees a nonempty index set.

comparison: For the selected coordinate set S, integrate the vector epsilon^(e)*x_S^(e) under each environment law, average uniformly over the nonempty finite environment set, then take its squared Euclidean norm. EuclideanSpace supplies the L2 norm rather than the supremum norm of an unwrapped finite function. The square is outside the pooled mean, so cross-environment cancellation remains and the expression is not the average of squared environment means. Required first/product moments must exist; any interpretation as a coefficient-bias bound from Remark 4.2 retains its S containing S* restriction and is not part of this scalar definition.
gap: Vector integration and the Euclidean norm directly express the pooled bias measure, with averaging order and the source interpretation domain retained.
searches: Inspect EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and the Bochner integral against b_S
The norm formula confirms the squared L2 norm after averaging; it does not commute a square with the environment average or establish a coefficient-bias identity.

comparison: Model independent time-indexed FULL vectors (X,Y^(1),...,Y^(K)) with common law Q and rewards in [0,1], then specify the armwise conditional expectation given X as f_k^Q(X). This does not require reward coordinates to be independent within a vector. Bounded measurable rewards on a probability space are integrable, permitting the conditional-mean representation with its almost-everywhere version qualification. Only the selected arm reward is observed; the potential full reward vector is not policy information. A history-dependent policy needs the correct pre-reward information and current X when using Adapted; do not make it measurable with respect to a filtration that already reveals the current rewards. The generic adaptedness predicate does not create the permitted history or prove the displayed covariate-only conditional mean extends to a selected-action conditional mean without the model independence assumptions.
gap: Independent laws, conditional expectation and adaptedness support the model after the observed-history filtration and reward-function versions are specified.
searches: Inspect iIndepFun, IdentDistrib, condExp and Adapted:55-61 against the target reward model and policy observation scope
The primitives encode independent full vectors and conditional means but do not authorize observing unselected rewards or including current rewards in the action-selection filtration.

comparison: Impose the two inequalities on Q_X mass of closed SUP-norm balls centered at each point of the target measure support, for every real 0<r<=1, with one pair of constants qbar>qunder>0. Metric.closedBall uses the ambient distance; use the coordinate supremum metric or the inherited metric on the covariate domain, not the Euclidean L2 metric without changing constants. Measure.support is the topological measure support, not the support of a density function or observed sample. This is a small-ball mass assumption as printed, not merely the existence of an everywhere bounded Lebesgue density; do not drop the support/domain geometry or extrapolate it to all radii. Probability finiteness justifies real mass conversion, but does not prove either bound.
gap: Closed balls and measure support express the mass bounds directly once the source's supremum metric and covariate domain are used.
searches: Inspect closedBall:419-425 and Measure.support:54-59 against the two-sided small-ball mass condition
Both primitives match the geometric objects, but the ambient metric, support-restricted centers and radius interval remain essential parts of the source condition.
